run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T05:12:01Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is explained by a burst of HTTP 500s on the frontend's /api/data route between roughly 05:13Z and 05:22Z, and every failing request in that burst failed on its call to the ad service: the frontend's client spans for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds ended with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 UNAVAILABLE and grpc.error_message 'No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' (the ad Service ClusterIP). The trigger was a rollout restart of Deployment otel-demo/ad at 2026-11-17T05:13:21Z (new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5, template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:13:21Z). The new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh's container started and was reported Ready at 05:13:23Z and the old pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc was stopped at 05:13:23Z, but the ad container's own log shows it only began starting at 05:18:10.907Z and only 'started, listening on 8080' at 05:20:06.209Z. Because the ad Deployment's pod template defines no readiness probe, the not-yet-listening replacement was treated as a ready endpoint while the only serving pod had already been removed, so the ad Service had no listener and frontend calls were refused. Frontend GetAds error spans stop and ad server-side GetAds traffic resumes right after the listener came up (errors 0 from 05:24:00Z onward). Affected entities for which I observed their own failure evidence: frontend-proxy (own ingress / router frontend egress ERROR spans, 6.33% ingress error ratio at 05:18:00Z), frontend (own 500 error spans on GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds), and the ad workload's serving pod (Ready from 05:13:23Z but no listening socket until 05:20:06Z, server-side GetAds spans at 0 in 05:16–05:21). Sampled traces also show load-generator spans with http.status_code=500 for the same requests. Checked and not failing on this path: frontend's client calls to CartService, CheckoutService, ProductCatalogService and RecommendationService had no ERROR spans in the window, and the ad service's own server spans carried no error status (the failure was transport-level, not the ad app rejecting calls). The adFailure='on' flag in ConfigMap flagd-config declares 'Fail ad service' but does not match the observed failure path and is rejected as the cause. The fraud-detection container's last termination (OOMKilled, 04:47:59Z) predates the alert onset and is not tied to this path. Unknowns: what/who initiated the rollout restart at 05:13:21Z (change history is not integrated), why the ad JVM took ~4m47s to start logging and ~6m43s to listen (84% CFS throttling of the new container is consistent but not proof), and the alert rule definition/evaluation history (list_prometheus_rules returned no rule data). Note the alert's stated start (05:12:01Z) is ~80s before the rollout and the first large error burst; small numbers of frontend-proxy ingress ERROR spans (1.3–2.7 per 2m) existed earlier in the window, so the exact alert-triggering instant is not observable from the available data.

claims.text: frontend-proxy recorded 427.2 ingress spans and 393.7 'router frontend egress' spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR in the 84-minute window, while carrying ~24,400 non-error spans on each operation, i.e. its request path to the frontend was returning errors at a small but sustained fraction.
The frontend-proxy ingress error ratio (ERROR / all ingress spans over a 5m rate) was 6.33% at 2026-11-17T05:18:00Z, confirming the alerting signal was elevated during the incident.

Over 04:12–05:36 the frontend's ERROR spans were confined to the ads path: GET /api/data 393.5, executing api route (pages) /api/data 393.5, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 393.6 and tcp.connect 15.2; its CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and RecommendationService/ListRecommendations client spans had 0 ERROR spans in the same query.

Sampled traces from 05:16:25Z show frontend 'GET /api/data' spans with http.status_code=500 and a child span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds with otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=14, whose grpc.error_message is '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080'; the same traces contain frontend-proxy ingress and 'router frontend egress' spans with http.status_code=500 and load-generator spans with http.status_code=500.
100.70.197.56 is the ClusterIP of Service ad in namespace otel-demo, whose port 8080 targets container port 8080; its current endpoint is pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh (pod IP 100.96.3.224).

Events in otel-demo show Deployment ad scaling up ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 from 0 to 1 at 05:13:21Z, the new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh scheduled/pulled/created/started at 05:13:21–05:13:23Z, and Deployment ad scaling down ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0 with pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc 'Stopping container ad' at 05:13:23Z (ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete at the same times).

ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 (deployment revision 2) carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:13:21Z, i.e. the ad Deployment was restarted with a rollout restart at that time; its visible container spec otherwise matches ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, same env, same ports, same resources).

The ad Deployment's pod template has readinessProbe null and livenessProbe null, uses RollingUpdate maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, and limits the ad container to cpu 50m / memory 450Mi; the replacement pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh was therefore marked Ready at 05:13:23Z (same minute its container started, restartCount 0) although the application was not yet listening.

The replacement ad container's own log shows 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-17T05:18:10.90717568Z and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 2026-11-17T05:20:06.208743196Z, i.e. no listener on port 8080 from the old pod's termination at 05:13:23Z until 05:20:06Z.

Minute-resolution series show frontend GetAds ERROR spans from 05:16:00Z through 05:23:00Z (peaks 152–158.7 per 2m), ad's server-side oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans at 1.33 then 0 from 05:17:00Z to 05:21:00Z, ad server spans resuming at 82.03 (05:22:00Z) and 140 (05:23:00Z), and frontend GetAds ERROR spans falling to 20 (05:23:00Z) then 0 from 05:24:00Z, while frontend's successful (UNSET) GetAds spans resume from 05:22:00Z.

The new ad container was CPU-throttled in 0.839 of its CFS periods over the window, versus 0.156 for the old ad pod's container, consistent with the 50m CPU limit delaying JVM startup and binding of port 8080.
ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo contains flag adFailure with defaultVariant 'on' (description 'Fail ad service'), alongside other fault-injection flags whose defaults are 'off'.

The fraud-detection container in pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zzt65 has restartCount 1 with lastState terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-17T04:47:59Z, and has been running since 04:47:59Z.

The ad service's own server spans for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds never carried ERROR status in the window (only STATUS_CODE_UNSET), and frontend's client calls to CartService, CheckoutService, ProductCatalogService and RecommendationService had 0 ERROR spans; the failures are transport-level connection refusals on the ad path, not the ad app returning error statuses or a broad frontend failure.

The flagd flag adFailure='on' ('Fail ad service') is not the cause of this alert: the observed failure was TCP connection refusal at the ad Service ClusterIP before any request reached the ad process, ad's own GetAds server spans show no error status, and ad serves ~130–140 successful GetAds spans per 2m from 05:23:00Z onward while the flag value is still 'on' in the ConfigMap captured at query time.

The fraud-detection container's OOMKill is not the cause of the frontend-proxy error alert: that termination (exit 137, OOMKilled) finished at 04:47:59Z, before the alert onset at 05:12:01Z and before the 05:13–05:22 error burst, and no fraud-detection/checkout error spans were observed in the window.

The replacement ad container's slow start (first startup log 4m47s after container start and listener only 6m43s after it) is plausibly caused by its 50m CPU limit combined with JVM startup, since 83.9% of its CFS periods were throttled; this is a supported-but-unproven contributing factor rather than an observed cause.

Add a readiness/startup probe (e.g. gRPC health check on port 8080) to the ad Deployment so a replacement pod is not added to the ad Service endpoints before it listens, and consider maxUnavailable: 0 with adequate maxSurge or a startupProbe covering JVM startup; this removes the single-replica outage on every ad rollout.

Identify who/what performed the rollout restart of Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T05:13:21Z (change history is not integrated in this Run) and check whether the ad CPU limit of 50m is appropriate for its JVM startup.

gaps: Change history is not integrated, so what or who triggered the kubectl rollout restart of Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T05:13:21Z (annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) is unknown.

The RequestErrorRate alert rule definition and its evaluation history are unavailable: list_prometheus_rules returned no rule data (rule_name RequestErrorRate and an unfiltered query both returned no_data), so the exact instant the rule first exceeded threshold and the meaning of 'current: 2.4555555555555553' cannot be verified.

The alert's stated start (05:12:01Z) precedes the ad rollout (05:13:21Z) by ~80s; frontend-proxy ingress ERROR spans of 1.3–2.7 per 2m were already present earlier in the window (e.g. 05:06–05:13), so the alert onset cannot be tied precisely to the burst from the available data.

Why the replacement ad container produced no startup log until 05:18:10.907Z and only bound port 8080 at 05:20:06.209Z is not proven; the 83.9% CFS throttling ratio and the 50m CPU limit are consistent but correlate only.
flagd logs for 05:10–05:25 were not obtained (the fetch_pod_logs query for flagd-5466bf5bc-jfcxr returned no lines), so flagd's condition during the ad restart is unknown.
A networkpolicies query in namespace otel-demo returned no objects; that result is not citable as proof that no policy exists or existed, so network policy is neither confirmed nor excluded.

The fraud-detection container has an event 'Created container: fraud-detection' at 05:20:11Z, which does not match its recorded lastState (OOMKilled, finishedAt 04:47:59Z, running since 04:47:59Z); this discrepancy is unexplained and fraud-detection's own health at 05:20 is not established.

Services whose own error/latency signals I did not examine (cart, checkout, currency, product-catalog, shipping, email, accounting, quote, image-provider, kafka, payment) cannot be declared healthy; only the absence of ERROR spans on frontend's client calls to some of them was observed.
next_steps: Review the audit/change log (outside this Run) for the kubectl rollout restart of Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T05:13:21Z and for any flagd-config edits around 05:05–05:13.
Add a readiness/startup probe to the ad Deployment container (and/or maxUnavailable: 0) and re-evaluate its 50m CPU limit so single-replica rollouts do not remove the only listening backend.
Check the RequestErrorRate rule definition/evaluation outside this Run to confirm the exact threshold and window behind the 05:12:01Z alert start.

If the adFailure flag in flagd-config is not intentionally 'on', confirm whether it should be reset, and verify whether the ad service actually evaluates it (ad's ResolveBoolean/resolve span counts were 0 throughout the window).
